title: The weak thin shell conjecture for log-concave random vectors
statement:
Let $X$ be a log-concave random vector, let $|\cdot|_2$ denote the Euclidean norm, and define its weak $p$-moment by

$$
\sigma_p(X)=\sup_{|z|_2\le1}\left(\mathbb{E}|\langle z,X\rangle|^p\right)^{1/p}.
$$

**Weak thin shell conjecture.** There exists $c>0$ such that for every log-concave random vector $X$,

$$
\forall\,p\ge1,\qquad \left(\mathbb{E}|X|_2^p\right)^{1/p}\le\mathbb{E}|X|_2+c\,\sigma_p(X).
$$

This seeks to remove the multiplicative constant in the known strong-versus-weak moment estimate for log-concave vectors. It is presented as a weaker consequence suggested by the thin shell conjecture; no resolution is given.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1203.0893](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0893).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1204

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).
source_name: Olivier Guédon, “Concentration phenomena in high dimensional geometry”, arXiv:1310.1204 (2013).
